Status: Wave 284 accepted (6.3): the Falcon property-description model

Method.evidence: Class881 is the property-description frame wrapper and Class876 its property-request base. Both directions of the model conversion are explicit in the IL: Class881::a() (ToPropertyDescription) builds a Knx.Falcon.PropertyDescription from eleven getters, and Class881::a(PropertyDescription) (FromPropertyDescription) writes all eleven fields from that description, so the two bodies are a complete field-to-property table. The 11-argument constructor names its parameters in that exact order - objectType, instance, propertyId, propertyIndex, propertyDataType, writeEnabled, maxSize, readRights, writeRights, mainDpt, subDpt - and the already accepted get_WriteEnabled sits at position six, which validates the positional pairing. Each accessor also lands on the frame offset its sibling uses (offset 5/6 property index, 11 property data type, 12 max size, 14 s two nibbles read/write rights, 7 main DPT, 9 sub DPT), and GetFormattedData prints the same frame as PropertyIndex={0} DataType={1} MaxSize={2}. Class876::c/b/a are the objectType/instance/propertyId getters and their ushort setters the matching writers. The byte[] factory only wraps the caller buffer, the same shape as the family s UnsafeFromBuffer.
Method.themes: A model-conversion pair is a naming table: two methods that convert between a frame wrapper and its DTO name every field in one read, and the DTO constructor parameter names confirm each position. Two Class881 rows stay unresolved - method_25 and c(byte) touch the high nibble of the property-index byte pair but are used by neither conversion, so their packing is not evidenced yet.
